text:
Hi everyone,
I finished my gradual process (STUPRO) and have been an Israeli citizen for about 2.5 years.
My brother is planning to visit Israel soon together with his partner. His partner is coming for a business trip, and my brother is joining to travel a bit and visit me.
Some background:
* My brother holds a Belarusian passport, but he has been living in the Netherlands for last 3 or 4 years on a Dutch partnership residence permit.
* He visited me once before in 2022 (right after the war in Ukraine broke out). At that time, we didn’t arrange an advance permit; he was held at Ben Gurion border control for about 6 hours for questioning, but was ultimately allowed in and left on time after one week.
* Years ago, when my mom visited, I had to formally submit an invitation via Misrad HaPnim, but back then I was still in the gradual process on temporary status, where advance approval is strictly mandatory.

**My question: **Now that I am a full Israeli citizen, do I still need/is it advisable to go through Misrad HaPnim to get an official advance entry permit/guarantee for him?
Or is it sufficient for him to apply for ETA-IL (he already did it btw), bring proof of his Dutch residence permit/employment, return tickets, and an invitation letter directly from me? Given his past 6-hour delay at border control, I want to minimize the risk of issues at Natbag.
Would appreciate hearing recent experiences or advice from anyone who has invited first-degree relatives in a similar situation. 
Thanks in advance!
